obligations.note: The change introduces FX_RATES_URL = "http://fx.fernbrook.example/rates" and a new fx_rate() function that calls outbound._transport.send() against this HTTP endpoint. ENC-2 requires every outbound integration endpoint to use HTTPS; this is a clear HTTP (not HTTPS) outbound call, directly violating the obligation.

The new FX service endpoint (fx.fernbrook.example) is not listed in controls/payments/asset-inventory.json, which only enumerates core-banking, sanctions-screening, and statement-delivery. INV-1 requires every outbound integration to be inventoried with an owner and data classification; this integration has neither.

Ticket CHG-25066 is approved by change manager Erik Brandt and its components list includes payments.payments, which is the component for the changed file payments.py per controls/payments/components.json.
Sofia Santos (change_approver for payments, payments-eng team) provided a code_review approval for the exact head commit bfec8e0; she is a different person from author Linh Nguyen.
The single code_review approval names commit bfec8e0775b49522f779eff68f00dc2c1ee59300, which is the only (and final) commit in the change; no later commits exist to void it.

CI ran on the final commit bfec8e0 with 172 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped. All registered control tests for obligations whose scope includes payments.py (PAY-1, PAY-2, MC-1) are present and passing.
The changed file payments.py maps to component payments.payments, which is not marked security_sensitive in controls/payments/components.json, so CHG-5 is not triggered.
The diff touches only apps/baseline-payments/payments/payments.py; no protected paths under controls/, ci/, or the test-controls directories are modified.
The ticket type is 'standard', not 'emergency', so the emergency post-implementation review requirement does not apply.
No exception is invoked or needed for this change; the existing exceptions in the register are unrelated to the FX rate feature.

The diff is purely additive (new constant and function inserted between release and _send_disbursement); the covered symbols required_approvals and release in the acceptance ledger (ACR-0401, ACR-0403) are unmodified, so prior evidence is not lapsed.

required_approvals and is_fully_approved in payments.py are unchanged by the diff; the exhaustive proof record (ACR-0401) and the passing CI control test confirm dual-control thresholds still match policy.
The release function in payments.py is unchanged; the Ponens trace (ACR-0403) and the passing CI test confirm idempotent release behaviour is preserved.
The approve and is_fully_approved functions in payments.py are not modified by the diff; the exhaustive CI control test passes, confirming maker-checker separation is intact.

summary: The change introduces a new outbound FX rate lookup function that calls an HTTP (not HTTPS) endpoint at fx.fernbrook.example, directly violating ENC-2's requirement that every outbound integration use TLS. The new integration is also absent from the approved asset inventory, violating INV-1. Both are critical-severity obligations and the violations are unambiguous from the diff. All process obligations (CHG-1 through CHG-7, EXC-1, LAP-1) and the unmodified payment-control obligations (PAY-1, PAY-2, MC-1) are satisfied. The change must be rejected and reworked to use an HTTPS endpoint and register the integration in the asset inventory before resubmission.
